thread:
customer-acme: Hey team — our production app started returning a bunch of 429s and some 401s this morning around 07:11 UTC. We also saw an unexpected billing spike. Using model rwd3-64k (hosted) from a single API key. Traffic pattern: many concurrent interactive sessions, short prompts then long completions (avg 4k tokens). Any ideas?

jess_support: Sorry about that — we'll help triage. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces the issue and the response headers you got (especially any Retry-After / X-RateLimit-* headers)? Also which endpoint (completion/chat/streaming) and region?

customer-acme: Here's an anonymized repro curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd3-64k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize..."}],"max_tokens":8000}'
```
Response headers (copied):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 07:11:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1765504675
```
Body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":"rate_limit"} 
We also saw a 401 once: {"error":"invalid_api_key"} but that was probably a key rotation on our side. Billing spike shows token counts jumped 3x at the same time window.

sam_engineer: Thanks — couple of quick checks: 1) are you reusing the same connection/HTTP client or creating many short-lived clients? 2) what's your concurrency level (requests in flight)? 3) are you doing synchronous blocking across many user sessions?

customer-acme: We have ~150 active sessions, and at peak about 90 concurrent outgoing requests to Redwood. We open a new connection per user in our current node server.

jess_support: That explains some behavior. A few things to consider: 1) model-specific limits: some larger variants have per-customer soft RPM/TPM and soft concurrency caps to protect multi-tenant capacity. The X-RateLimit headers you pasted show Limit=1200 and Remaining=0 — you hit the RPM window. 2) concurrency limits are enforced separately; if you open 90 concurrent requests and the model's concurrency per-customer is lower, requests can be queued or rejected with 429. 3) long context / large max_tokens increases per-request token accounting, so a few concurrent long requests will balloon TPM quickly.

marco_infra: Add on from infra: we saw an ingestion spike at 07:11:10 UTC coming from your API key IP range — ~220 reqs in a 10s window with many large context sizes. The serving pool for rwd3-64k had to throttle to maintain latency SLO; some requests were returned 429 with Retry-After 3s. We didn't see internal auth fails. The single 401 likely came from an expired key on your side.

jess_support: Immediate mitigation steps you can try: 
- Reduce concurrency: implement a client-side concurrency cap (e.g., 20 in-flight requests) and queue at app level.
- Reuse HTTP connections / keep-alive to avoid socket churn.
- Reduce max_tokens where possible or split long outputs into streaming chunked responses.
- Respect Retry-After header + exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., base 200ms -> 2s -> 4s).
- Check billing: long outputs cost more tokens; errant loop could cause the spike.

customer-acme: Can you confirm what the per-model soft limits are for rwd3-64k (RPM/TPM/concurrency)? We need concrete numbers to tune our client.

sam_engineer: I can't post exact global soft caps in public thread, but we can share safe tuning targets: for heavy models like 64k variants, assume effective per-key concurrency target <= 30 and plan RPM bursts under 1000 with smoothing. If you need higher steady capacity, we can propose Dedicated capacity or an increased quota.

jess_support: Also check response headers for `X-Model-Concurrency-Limit` or similar — some endpoints return per-model concurrency and current queue depth in headers. If you can capture a 429 response with full headers and paste here we can be precise.

customer-acme: Got one with more headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 4
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1765504680
X-Model-Concurrency-Max: 40
X-Model-Concurrency-Current: 42
```
That X-Model-Concurrency-* looks telling. We were at 42 > 40.

marco_infra: Yep that matches server-side queue overflow. We return X-Model-Concurrency-Max to indicate soft per-key concurrency cap. When Current > Max we either queue (if queue not full) or return 429.

jess_support: Repro steps we suggest for your infra team:
1) Run a local load test hitting the same endpoint with same tokens/context: we use this script internally:
```bash
# minimal loadgen example (bash + curl, parallel n)
for i in $(seq 1 80); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd3-64k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}],"max_tokens":5000}' &
done
wait
```
2) Capture headers and per-request latencies. 3) Lower concurrent count until X-Model-Concurrency-Current <= X-Model-Concurrency-Max and token RPM stays below RateLimit.

customer-acme: That loadgen reproduces 429s locally, good. If we implement a global queueed worker pool on our side (cap 25) do you think we'll be OK at our current traffic level?

sam_engineer: Likely yes for short bursts — but token TPM still matters. With 25 in-flight requests of ~4k tokens each, TPM will be high. We recommend two-pronged approach: limit concurrency to 25 + reduce max_tokens per request when possible or move to streaming and stitch outputs. Also add jittered exponential backoff and a local retry budget per user to avoid thundering herd.

billing-bot: FYI I pulled the billing window for your API key: token consumption spiked from ~600k tokens/hour to ~1.9M tokens/hour during the 07:10–07:15 UTC window. That explains the invoice variance. If you want we can issue a one-time usage report and map tokens to request IDs.

customer-acme: Yes please send the per-request usage export and also confirm whether Dedicated capacity would avoid these soft throttles.

marco_infra: Dedicated would provide reserved slots and higher concurrency guarantees; we'd need to size GPUs and negotiate commit. For short term, smoothing on the client is fastest. For long term, we can schedule a call to discuss Dedicated sizing.

jess_support: I'll create a follow-up ticket to 1) send a usage export, 2) attach recommended client-side code snippets, and 3) propose Dedicated sizing options. In the ticket we'll include the raw headers you pasted and the loadgen results.

customer-acme: Thanks — one more question: we sometimes see 401s interleaved. Is that ever caused by rate limits?

sam_engineer: Not normally. 401 is auth; ensure keys aren't being rotated mid-flight and that clock skew isn't causing JWT validation issues. 429/401 could appear close together if your client is retrying with a rotated key.

customer-acme: Understood. We'll implement the concurrency cap + keep-alive + backoff today and report back. Appreciate the help.

ops-bot: [automated] Escalation created: INC-2026-1287 assigned to infra for follow-up (includes headers & loadgen logs).

jess_support: Closing the thread here but I'll post the usage export into the ticket and follow-up with Dedicated options. Feel free to ping if you see other anomalous error patterns. :thumbsup:
